--- title: "Touring multivariate data" --- ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Error in library(fiftystater) : there is no package called 'fiftystater' ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ## Pairwise plots :::: columns ::: column ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](08-mvplot-tour_files/figure-revealjs/scatterplot matrix-1.png){fig-align='center' width=576} ::: ::: ::: ::: column What don't you see?

Unless you have tours, you'll never know 🫣 ::: :::: ## Our first tour {.smaller} `What patterns do you see?`{=html} ::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"} ``{=html} ::: ::: columns ::: column ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # Run the tour animate_xy(penguins_std[,2:5], col=penguins_std$species, axes="off", fps=10) ``` ::: What new things do we learn? - The separation between clusters is larger and - there are a few more unusual penguins. ::: ::: column ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ![](images/penguins2d.gif) ::: ::: ## What did you see? {.inverse} ::: incremental - clusters ✅ - outliers ✅ - linear dependence ✅ - elliptical clusters with slightly different shapes ✅ - separated elliptical clusters with slightly different shapes ✅ ::: ## Which shows better separation? ::: columns ::: column ![](images/penguins2d.gif) ::: ::: column ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](08-mvplot-tour_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## What is a tour? {.smaller} ::: columns ::: column - a movie of low-dim projections - constructed to come close to showing all possible low-dim projections - a grand tour is a space-filling curve in the manifold of low-dim projections of high-dim data spaces. ![](images/hands.png){width="80%"} ::: ::: {.column width="5%"} ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} ${\mathbf x}_i \in \mathcal{R}^p$, $i^{th}$ data vector $F$ is a $p\times d$ orthonormal basis $F'F=I_d$, where $d$ is the projection dimension. The projection of ${\mathbf x_i}$ onto $F$ is ${\mathbf y}_i=F'{\mathbf x}_i$. Tour is indexed by time, $F(t)$, where $t\in [a, z]$. Starting and target frame denoted as $F_a = F(a), F_z=F(t)$. The animation of the projected data is given by a path ${\mathbf y}_i(t)=F'(t){\mathbf x}_i$. ::: ::: ## Geodesic interpolation b/w planes ::: columns ::: column Tour is indexed by time, $F(t)$, where $t\in [a, z]$. Starting and target frame denoted as $F_a = F(a), F_z=F(t)$. The animation of the projected data is given by a path ${\mathbf y}_i(t)=F'(t){\mathbf x}_i$. ::: ::: column ![](images/geodesic.png){width="120%"} ::: ::: ## Reading axes - interpretation Length and direction of axes relative to the pattern of interest ![](images/reading_axes.001.png){width="100%"} ## Reading axes - interpretation Length and direction of axes relative to the pattern of interest ![](images/reading_axes.002.png){width="100%"} ## Understanding a tour {.smaller} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ## Understanding the projections {.smaller} ::: columns ::: column ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(penguins_std, aes(x=fl, y=bd, colour=species)) + geom_point(alpha=0.7, size=2) + scale_colour_discrete_divergingx(palette = "Zissou 1") + theme(aspect.ratio=1, legend.position="bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](08-mvplot-tour_files/figure-revealjs/runthis1-1.png){fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: Gentoo from others in contrast of fl, bd ::: ::: column ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(penguins_std, aes(x=bl, y=bm, colour=species)) + geom_point(alpha=0.7, size=2) + scale_colour_discrete_divergingx(palette = "Zissou 1") + theme(aspect.ratio=1, legend.position="bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](08-mvplot-tour_files/figure-revealjs/runthis2-1.png){fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: Chinstrap from others in contrast of bl, bm ::: ::: ## Difficulties in making interpretations - There may be multiple and different combinations of variables that reveal similar structure. ☹️ - This is due to association between variables in the multivariate data. - The tour can help to discover these, too. 😂 ## Other tour types {.smaller} - [guided]{.orange}: follows the optimisation path for a projection pursuit index. - [little]{.orange}: interpolates between all variables. - [local]{.orange}: rocks back and forth from a given projection, so shows all possible projections within a radius. - [dependence]{.orange}: two independent 1D tours - [frozen]{.orange}: fixes some variable coefficients, others vary freely. - [manual]{.orange}: control coefficient of one variable, to examine the sensitivity of structure this variable. (In the [`spinifex`]{.orange} package) - [slice]{.orange}: use a section instead of a projection. - [sage]{.orange}: transform a 2D projection, to avoid data piling. ## Guided tour {.smaller} New target bases are chosen using a projection pursuit index function $$\mathop{\text{maximize}}_{F}~g(xF) ~~~\text{ subject to } F \text{ being orthonormal}$$ - `holes`: This is an inverse Gaussian filter, which is optimised when there is not much data in the center of the projection, i.e. a "hole" or donut shape in 2D. - `central mass`: The opposite of holes, high density in the centre of the projection, and often "outliers" on the edges. - `LDA`/`PDA`: An index based on the linear discriminant dimension reduction (and penalised), optimised by projections where the named classes are most separated. ## ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Grand ![](images/penguins2d.gif){width="80%"} Might accidentally see best separation ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} Guided, using LDA index ![](images/penguins2d_guided.gif){width="80%"} Moves to the best separation ::: ::: ## Manual tour {.smaller} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} - start from best projection, given by projection pursuit - `bd` contribution controlled - if `bd` is removed from projection, Gentoo separation disappears - `bd` is important for distinguishing Gentoo ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # Check contribution of bl, # change mvar to switch variables animate_xy(penguins_std[,2:5], radial_tour(as.matrix(best_proj), mvar = 2), col = penguins_std$species) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](images/penguins_rt_bd.gif){width="90%"} ::: ::: ## Manual tour {.smaller} ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} - start from best projection, given by projection pursuit - `bl` contribution controlled - `bl` is important for distinguishing Adelie from Chinstrap ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](images/penguins_rt_bl.gif){width="90%"} ::: ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ## Local Tour {.smaller} ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Rocks from and to a given projection, in order to observe the neighbourhood ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](images/penguins2d_local.gif){width="90%"} ::: ::: ## Geometric shapes with slice tour {.smaller} ::: columns ::: {.column width="45%"} Solid 4D sphere ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(geozoo) sphere2 <- sphere.solid.random(p=4)$points %>% as_tibble() animate_slice(sphere2, axes="bottomleft") ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ![](images/sphere4d_solid_slice.gif){width="70%"} ::: ::: {.column width="5%"} ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} Hollow 4D sphere ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} sphere1 <- sphere.hollow(p=4)$points %>% as_tibble() animate_slice(sphere1, axes="bottomleft", half_range=0.6) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ![](images/sphere4d_slice.gif){width="70%"} ::: ::: ## Geometric shapes with slice tour {.smaller} ::: columns ::: {.column width="45%"} 4D Torus ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} torus <- torus(p = 4, n = 5000, radius=c(8, 4, 1))$points %>% as_tibble() animate_slice(torus, axes="bottomleft", half_range=0.8) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ![](images/torus4d_slice.gif){width="70%"} ::: ::: {.column width="5%"} ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} 4D Hollow Cube ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} cube1 <- cube.face(p=4)$points %>% as_tibble() # Slicing needs data to be on a standard scale cube1_std <- cube1 %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ scale(.)[,1])) animate_slice(cube1_std, axes="bottomleft") ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ![](images/cube4d_slice.gif){width="70%"} ::: ::: ## PCA tour {.smaller} ::: columns ::: {.column width="45%"} Compute PCA, reduce dimension, show original variable axes in the reduced space. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins_pca <- prcomp(penguins_std[,2:5], center = FALSE) penguins_coefs <- penguins_pca$rotation[, 1:3] penguins_scores <- penguins_pca$x[, 1:3] animate_pca(penguins_scores, pc_coefs = penguins_coefs, col=penguins_std$species) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} render_gif( penguins_scores, grand_tour(), display_pca(pc_coefs = penguins_coefs, col=penguins_std$species, axes="bottomleft"), "slides/images/penguins2d_pca.gif", frames=100, width=400, height=400) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="5%"} ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} ![](images/penguins2d_pca.gif){width="100%"} ::: ::: ## Projection dimension and displays {.smaller} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} 1D projections displayed as a density ![](images/penguins1d.gif){width="80%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} animate_dist_cl(penguins_std[,2:5], half_range=1.3) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} Density contours overlaid on a scatterplot ![](images/penguins2d_dens.gif){width="80%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} animate_density2d( penguins_std[,2:5], col=penguins_std$species, axes="bottomleft") ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Your turn {.inverse} Using the sample code from the tour package, check how many clusters are in the example data. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tourr) data(flea) ?animate_xy # On a Mac, start quartz window with: quartz() # On windows, start X11 window with: X11() animate_xy(flea[, 1:6]) # RStudio graphics windows: may want to reduce frame rate animate_xy(flea[, 1:6], fps=10) # Also animate_xy(flea[, -7], col = flea$species) animate_xy(flea[, 1:6], tour_path = guided_tour(lda_pp(flea$species)), col=flea$species) ``` ::: ::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Saving and sharing: Animated gif ::: columns ::: column ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} render_gif( penguins_std[,2:5], grand_tour(), display_xy( col=penguins_std$species, axes="bottomleft"), gif_file="slides/images/penguins2d.gif", frames=100, width=400, height=400 ) ``` ::: ::: ::: column ![](images/penguins2d.gif){width="100%"} ::: ::: ## Saving and sharing: single frame {.smaller} ::: columns ::: column Draw it with ggplot, and possibly pass to plotly. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} load(here::here("data/p_tour_path.rda")) penguins_pcti <- interpolate( penguins_pct, 0.2) f27 <- matrix( penguins_pcti[,,27], ncol=2) p27 <- render_proj( penguins_std[,2:5], f27, obs_labels= penguins_std$species) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: ::: column ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Resources {.smaller} - [Cook and Laa (2025)](https://dicook.github.io/mulgar_book/) - [Emerson et al (2013) The Generalized Pairs Plot, JCGS, 22:1, 79-91](https://doi.org/10.1080/10618600.2012.694762) - [Natalia da Silva](http://natydasilva.com/): [PPForest](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/PPforest/index.html) and [shiny app](https://natydasilva.shinyapps.io/shinyV03/). - [Wickham et al (2011) tourr: An R Package for Exploring Multivariate Data with Projections](https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v040i02/v40i02.pdf), [tourr R package](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/tourr/index.html) - [Schloerke et al (2016) Escape from Boxland](https://journal.r-project.org/archive/2016/RJ-2016-044/index.html), [the web site zoo](http://schloerke.com/geozoo/) and [geozoo R package](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/geozoo/index.html) - [Spyrison and Cook (2020). spinifex: Manual Tours, Manual Control of Dynamic Projections of Numeric Multivariate Data.](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/spinifex/index.html) - Stuart Lee [liminal](https://github.com/sa-lee/liminal): tools to do linked brushing between tours and PCA/tSNE/PDS views ::: bottom This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
